title: DREAM: LLM-based Dynamic Role-playing via Event-Aware Memory Graph

problem.claim: Accurate role-playing requires stylistic imitation together with temporally consistent and causally grounded behavioral reasoning.

gap.claim: Existing role-playing agents rely mainly on static character descriptions and unstructured memory, limiting long-term narrative and personality coherence.

contributions.claim: DREAM is a structured memory framework for role-playing agents inspired by the Activating Event–Belief–Consequence cognitive model.
DREAM transforms unstructured literary text into a temporally ordered and causally linked Event-aware Memory Graph.
The Temporal Causal Memory benchmark evaluates temporal consistency and long-range causal narrative coherence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: DREAM records either state-of-the-art or competitive performance on CoSER, LIFECHOICE, and TCM, exceeding multiple strong baselines.
The authors report that structured memory enhances the interpretability and consistency of role-playing agents.

narrative_sequence.summary: Role-playing agents are an important application of large language models.
Established-character role-playing requires stylistic, temporal, and causal behavioral fidelity.
Static descriptions and unstructured memory limit long-term narrative and personality coherence.
DREAM builds an event-aware memory graph and dynamic dual-granularity character profiles.
The approach is evaluated with TCM and reported to perform competitively across multiple benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The framework organizes character experiences as temporally ordered and causally linked events.

interpretation.claim: Explicit temporal and causal structure may support more coherent long-range behavioral reasoning than unstructured memory.

application.claim: For long-running character or agent systems, represent memory as linked events while retaining stable traits separately.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this representation improves performance outside the reported role-playing benchmarks.

unknowns: Benchmark metrics, dataset sizes, and quantitative results are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training procedure, or memory-construction algorithm.
The reported baselines and evaluation protocol are not identified.
